newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says framework set for punctual EMU in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says framework set for punctual EMU in 1999.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, a tireless advocate of European economic and monetary union (EMU), said on Monday that leaders of the 15-nation bloc laid the basis in 1996 to ensure a timely start for EMU in 1999.

In an article to appear in the economic daily Handelsblatt on Tuesday, Kohl wrote that decisions made at the European Union summit in Dublin earlier this month "ensure that European monetary union can begin punctually on January 1, 1999."

"After the decisions in Dublin we have come quite a bit closer to a united Europe," Kohl said, repeating his oft-stated conviction that bringing Europe closer together is a "question of fate" for Germany and the entire region.
By backing a "stability pact" to ensure fiscal discipline after EMU starts, EU leaders have made sure that the euro currency will be strong and stable and become a postive force for European union.
"The euro will be a lastingly stable and reliable currency," Kohl said.

Monetary union would provide a "vitamin boost" to the region's economy, making it possible for the single market to flourish and for the region's industry to reap the benefits of a market boasting 370 million consumers, he added.
Kohl said the German economy was well-placed in international competition. The economy began expanding again in 1996 and this growth was set to accelerate in 1997.
"But the unemployment development is cause for concern," he said. "The stimulation of the economy will not be sufficient to noticeably reduce the number of unemployed."
The government must continue its efforts to consolidate public budgets and German citizens must develop a new sense of independence and self-reliance.
"Young people who start their own businesses deserve our respect and encouragement," he said.
